routes.label: Enumerate side partitions and calculate circular-area differences
Bound using the two largest disks and attain equality

changes.rationale: Keep the extremal and circle-area targets with tangent and relative-circle-position support. Centers lie on the common perpendicular through A. On one side the disks are nested, while opposite-side interiors are disjoint. A side contributes the area of its largest disk minus its second-largest disk, or the whole area for a singleton. If radii 7 and 5 share a side, that side contributes 24*pi and the other side at most 9*pi, so the total is at most 33*pi. If they are opposite, their areas total 74*pi, but the radius-3 disk forces a subtraction of at least 9*pi. Thus S<=65*pi, attained by {7} opposite {1,3,5}, giving 49*pi+(25-9)*pi=65*pi, source D. Accept the reviewer's narrower sufficient route components, which explicitly retain the common circle-area and extremal scopes. Qualify the exclusion claim: p150's description broadly mentions sums/differences of learned figures, although its stated decomposition criterion is polygonal. It is unnecessary here; removing it avoids an uncertain curriculum-scope extension rather than proving that its description categorically excludes all circular combinations.

routes.label: Use a unit-circle polynomial and its conjugate

changes.rationale: Keep both complete alternatives and repair the optional symbolic-trigonometric assignment instead of discarding a valid route. With z=cos(x)+i*sin(x), P=f(z)=z^3-z^2+z+1 and |z|=1. Conjugate f(z)=0 and multiply by z^3 to obtain z^3+z^2-z+1=0. Subtracting the two equations gives 2*z*(1-z)=0; z cannot be zero, while z=1 has f(1)=2, so source A follows. The alternative imaginary part is sin(2*x)*(2*cos(x)-1). Derive this identity from the explicitly printed generic h070 difference formula plus reductions and unit-circle relations, using the separated-D symbolic reuse proof. Its zeros in [0,2*pi) are x=0,pi/2,pi,3*pi/2,pi/3,5*pi/3. The real parts are respectively 2,2,-2,2,1,1, all nonzero. The title-only h074 lookup does not resolve the issue: its actual scope is special-value simplification. Replace h071/h073 by the complete generic-formula derivation and unit-circle components; do not broaden their special-angle criteria or erase the mathematically valid second route.

routes.label: Use the component relation and written count subtraction

changes.rationale: Preserve the approved I28 candy mapping and its exact source A. The response patterns are YNN for truth-tellers, YYN for liars, and NNN or YYY for alternaters. Thus only truth-tellers account for the excess of first-question yes answers over second-question yes answers: 22-15=7. Each truth-teller receives one piece. The full count vector (truth-tellers,liars,YYY alternaters,NNN alternaters)=(7,6,9,9) totals 31 and reproduces yes counts 22,15,9. The approved finite-constraint and propositional-operation definitions resolve the frozen logic gap, with equation subtraction and written subtraction as separate optional routes. Preserve those roles and the individual AMC12 binding rather than making a particular arithmetic procedure universal.

records.reason: Retain the original roles and valid route identity; the accepted raw change only adjusts one route label. Write p(x)=(x-h)^2+k. If p has no real root then p(p(x)) has none; if it has one distinct root, that single target has at most two preimages. With two roots r<s, exactly three composition zeros require r=k and s>k, since target levels have 0,1 or 2 preimages according as they lie below, at or above the minimum k. Put t=sqrt(-k)>0. The roots are h-t,h+t, so h-t=k=-t^2 and h=t-t^2=1/4-(t-1/2)^2. This uniquely maximizes h at t=1/2. The sum of p's roots is 2*h and the sum of the three composition zeros is 3*h, so either possible root-sum reading gives the same optimizer. Thus p_tilde(x)=(x-1/4)^2-1/4 and p_tilde(1)=5/16, source A. Equivalently the relation (k-h)^2+k=0 has discriminant 1-4*h as an equation in k, giving the same bound and unique equality case. No source ambiguity changes the selected answer or grading.

routes.label: Develop the cone and prove a tangent-plus-arc lower bound

changes.rationale: Preserve the approved complete I28 frustum route and source E. The slant height is sqrt(27+9)=6. Cone similarity and its sector development give inner radius 6, outer radius 12 and period pi in developed angle; diametrically opposite endpoints differ by pi/2+k*pi. Reflect a lifted path if needed so its final angle is at least pi/2. It must first cross angle pi/3 at radius r>=6. Distance from A=(12,0) to that crossing has square (r-6)^2+108, so the initial path length is at least 6*sqrt(3). Radial projection of the remaining path to the radius-6 circle cannot increase length: for unit u,v and r,s>=6, |r*u-s*v|^2=(r-s)^2+r*s*|u-v|^2>=36*|u-v|^2. Apply this to path partitions; the projected angular travel is at least pi/6, so the remaining length is at least pi. The lower bound includes seam crossings and winding. It is attained by a tangent of length 6*sqrt(3) followed by an inner-rim arc of length pi, both within the annulus. Exact 258 supplies cone development; exact 141 only treats reflection-based broken-line problems and does not prove this obstacle path. The explicit projection proof supplies the missing optimality argument without assuming a new constrained-surface-path theorem.
